account: Shortly before 4 a.m. on Thursday 3 September 2026, Waymo pulled one of its driverless cars over in San Francisco's Richmond District. It had detected “a violation of our terms of service involving a firearm”. Waymo alerted emergency services and “cooperated fully” with police, a Waymo spokesperson told the Los Angeles Times (12 September). The San Francisco Police Department said officers made a “high-risk vehicle stop” and detained the two juvenile passengers. They found a loaded AR-style assault rifle, suspected marijuana and mace spray, and the two were taken to juvenile hall. The Independent, citing SFGATE, quotes SFPD spokesperson Allison Maxie calling the weapon an “AR-styled assault rifle also known as a ghost gun”. It says the boy and girl were booked into the Juvenile Justice Center on firearm-possession charges. The California Post puts the stop at 40th Avenue and Cabrillo Street. No source says how the firearm was detected; The Independent and Xataka both say this is unclear.

ai_role.statement: What the system did is established only at the level of the company. Waymo says it detected a terms-of-service violation involving a firearm, pulled the driverless car over and alerted emergency services. The Independent says it is not clear how the firearm was detected. Xataka says Waymo has not explained whether detection was automatic or human. The Monitor's statement that the vehicle's AI detected the gun is not supported by any cited source. The driverless car's ability to stop on command is the only system function the accounts describe.

fields.account: Shortly before 4 a.m. on Thursday 3 September 2026, Waymo pulled one of its driverless cars over in San Francisco's Richmond District. It had detected “a violation of our terms of service involving a firearm”. Waymo alerted emergency services and “cooperated fully” with police, a Waymo spokesperson told the Los Angeles Times (12 September). The San Francisco Police Department said officers made a “high-risk vehicle stop” and detained the two juvenile passengers. They found a loaded AR-style assault rifle, suspected marijuana and mace spray, and the two were taken to juvenile hall. The Independent, citing SFGATE, quotes SFPD spokesperson Allison Maxie calling the weapon an “AR-styled assault rifle also known as a ghost gun”. It says the boy and girl were booked into the Juvenile Justice Center on firearm-possession charges. The California Post puts the stop at 40th Avenue and Cabrillo Street. No source says how the firearm was detected; The Independent and Xataka both say this is unclear.
